body:
ANZU can already operate Windows applications, use Playwright with its own browser profile, and fetch public websites/APIs. It could not read or operate the owner's existing signed-in Chrome tab.

RFC-0217 adds an optional Manifest V3 extension and per-user Windows native messaging host. The owner explicitly shares a tab; ANZU's existing browser tool can read visible text, find excerpts, click/fill observed controls, and toggle basic ad blocking for that tab. Exact URL checks, fresh target IDs, command expiration, network permissions, and existing consequential-action approvals remain enforced. Navigation/disconnection revokes sharing and clears ad rules. No HTTP listener or owner API token is exposed.

Validation: 99 focused Python checks and four Node protocol/revocation checks passed. Real Chromium verified extension loading, page actions and ad-request block/unblock; a real native-host stdio round trip passed. Live ANZU tools enumerated 18 Windows application windows and fetched a public HTTPS page. PowerShell installer syntax and git diff checks passed. Full local pytest stalled at 28% in async fixture setup; stack inspection showed an asyncio wait and idle aiosqlite worker. The stalled run was stopped; no full local suite pass is claimed. Node checks are included in PR CI; browser smoke explicitly skips where Chromium is absent.

Install instructions: docs/chrome-connector.md. This does not upgrade the installed ANZU app. Owner-profile Chrome registration and live model-driven desktop control still require desktop acceptance. Basic ad blocking covers four advertising domains; publication to Chrome Web Store, full filter lists, iframe/shadow DOM and installer payload changes are outside this ticket. Architect-owned specifications are unchanged.
title: RFC-0217: Add ANZU connector for owner-shared Chrome tabs

body:
﻿Taco's request: the status banners on the ANZU Android home screen blocked the view. They now live in a **Notifications** tab.

**What moved off the screen**
- Desktop offline / "answering on this phone" banner (`CompanionOfflineStatus.offlineBannerText`), with **Pair desktop** or **Scan Wi-Fi**
- `state.error` cards. Every error the model reports becomes a dated event; permission errors offer **Open settings**
- The pending-confirmation card. **Retry safely**, and **Discard** behind the same confirmation as before
- Model and voice download failures (`localPackError`, `voicePackError`), with **Retry**. They are hidden while a retry runs.

The active-call controls card stays where it was; it is call controls, not a notice.

**How**
- `NoticeStore` on `JarvisApp` (SharedPreferences `anzu_notices`) is fed by **one** listener in `CompanionModel`: `NoticeRules.conditions(state, paired)` on every state change, plus one event per newly reported `state.error`. None of the ~35 error sites are touched.
- Live conditions update when their text changes and clear themselves when resolved. Their first-seen time and read/dismissed state persist, so a restart does not re-raise a notice you already read or dismissed. A dismissed condition comes back only if it changes or recurs.
- Events are dated and persisted, capped at 50 and dropped after 7 days. Identical repeats within 2 s are folded. They can be dismissed one by one or cleared with **Clear all**.
- Each card shows its time (localized), severity (Info/Warning/Error, colour plus label), an Ongoing tag for live conditions, its actions, and Dismiss. Actions are disabled while the app is busy.
- Home keeps only a small dot plus count in the header, which opens the tab. The tab's nav item has an unread badge. Opening the tab marks everything read.

**Strings:** new UI strings are in `values/strings_notifications.xml` with Dutch in `values-nl/`. The existing English-only `strings.xml` is marked `tools:ignore="MissingTranslation"`, so lint still checks the new file for missing Dutch. Notice bodies that come from the app (error messages, offline text) stay as the app writes them.

Personas and WebGL are not touched.

**Tests:** `NoticeStoreTest` (9) covers live conditions appearing and clearing, re-notifying on change, dismissed and read state surviving a restart, the event cap and age-out, folding repeats, dismiss and Clear all persisting, and the state-to-notice rules. `NotificationsScreenTest` (5, Compose) covers title, severity, body and the unread marker, actions including Discard's confirmation, Dismiss, Clear all, actions disabled while busy, the empty state, the Home indicator and Dutch strings.

VRPC (JDK 17, Kotlin in-process): `testDebugUnitTest lintDebug` green, 278 tests, 0 failures.

**Device check**
1. Open with no desktop: Home shows only the header dot and count, and Notifications shows "Desktop connection" with Pair desktop or Scan Wi-Fi.
2. Deny the mic: you get an Error event with Open settings.
3. Interrupt a model download (airplane mode): you get "Model download problem" with Retry. It clears once the download succeeds.
4. Dismiss and Clear all, then restart the app: dismissed items stay gone, and read items stay read.
5. Set the phone to Dutch: the tab reads "Meldingen".
title: android: Notifications tab — move Home status banners into one notice store (EN/NL)

QR creation waited indefinitely for the connectivity lock, including unrelated remote endpoint setup, and the browser fetch had no deadline. Reuse an already verified LAN gateway before waiting for the lock; bound lock acquisition to 3 seconds and gateway preparation to 25 seconds. Bound browser requests (including health checks and response reads) to 30 seconds and return actionable errors so the panel releases its busy state.

Scope: RFC-0213 pairing regression. Existing owner approval, gateway TLS pin, expiring codes, WAN settings, and security cooldown remain intact.

Validation: 31 backend pairing/security tests and 9 frontend recovery tests passed; frontend build/lint and git diff --check passed. Regression tests cover ready LAN ingress while the remote setup lock is held, bounded lock failure, and cancellation/lock release after a stalled gateway. Live installed desktop QR regeneration rendered successfully in 2.3 seconds. A deliberately stalled browser request hit the deadline and re-enabled buttons; normal QR rendering was restored afterward. Physical-phone scanning remains unverified.

Installed backend received only this pairing-method repair, preserving its existing UPnP implementation. Installed frontend was built with the avatar restoration from #623 retained. Backend restarted as a detached hidden process and health reports ok.
title: RFC-0213: prevent desktop QR creation from hanging

body:
## Summary

ANZU was asking for HexStrike permission too early. Selecting the HexStrike suite (ModelSelector / Appearance / a restored `localStorage` profile) called `POST /api/hexstrike/start`, which parks `cyber.hexstrike` (default `ask`) and shows the PermissionPrompt — including on what feels like startup when the last selected profile was HexStrike.

**This PR:** suite select only syncs the HUD profile. Permission is requested on the first **explicit** Start / Operate (unchanged backend gates), with clearer rationale copy.

## Investigation (startup prompt)

| Finding | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Not an Android runtime permission | No HexStrike entry in `AndroidManifest` / companion permission launchers |
| In-app computer-use grant | `cyber.hexstrike` in `computer_permissions.py`, default **`ask`**, gated on license module `hexstrike` |
| Trigger | `applyRuntimeProfile` → `startHexStrike()` → `POST /api/hexstrike/start` → `_require_operator_grant("cyber.hexstrike")` → HTTP 428 parked approval |
| Why "on startup" | Restored `jarvis_selected_runtime_profile` = hexstrike-suite (or selecting the suite) auto-started and parked the prompt |
| Explicit use paths (kept) | Daybreak **Start** button and **Operate** / chat operate still require the grant |

## Fix

- `applyRuntimeProfile`: HexStrike path only `syncRuntimeSelection`; does **not** call `/start`
- ModelSelector / Appearance copy: suite selected → user presses Start in Daybreak
- Rationale strings updated so the ask explains start/operate on this PC; command/payload/exploit endpoints remain blocked

## Out of scope (not in this PR)

**Command and payload options were not implemented.** Upstream HexStrike `/api/command` and payload routes stay denied by `_BLOCKED_TOKENS` in `backend/app/security/hexstrike.py` and by RFC-0048 / 0078 / 0079 / 0119. Operate already exposes discovered capabilities + JSON **arguments** in Daybreak. Opening raw command/payload/exploit proxying is refused (product + safety). No uncensored-worker workaround.

## Tests (VRPC)

- `pytest tests/test_computer_permissions.py` — **19 passed**
- `pytest tests/test_rfc0110_hexstrike_hardening.py` — **14 passed**
- Frontend `npm run lint` / Android `testDebugUnitTest` not run here (no `frontend/node_modules` in this worktree; change is HUD TS + Python policy, not Android)

## Head

`04fc5f33b3ef786f190aef9fc7654e8c79abeed4`

Do not merge until review.
title: fix(hexstrike): defer cyber.hexstrike permission until explicit start

body:
﻿Follow-up to #620: a voice-pack mirror of `running_download_locks_rows_and_refreshes_cannot_wipe_its_state`.

**Test** (`VoicePackDownloadRaceTest`, slowed MockWebServer download): while one STT pack downloads, refresh `VoicePackSource` + `refreshStatus()`, then start a second download that fails (same pack: already downloading; Pocket TTS: 404) through `VoicePackSource.update`. The running download must keep `DOWNLOADING`, stay in `downloadingPackIds()`, keep its progress, and finish installed at 100%. Covered for both the selected and an unselected STT pack.

**Bugs it exposed, fixed here** (`CompanionVoicePackManager`):
1. `refreshOne` only skipped when the *selected* pack was downloading; a download of an unselected pack of the same role had its `DOWNLOADING` status overwritten with `missing`. It now skips while any download of that role runs.
2. Download progress is one shared value; a second download reset it to 0 and wrote its own percentages. Progress is now owned by the first running download until it finishes.

VRPC (JDK 17): `testDebugUnitTest lintDebug` green, 266 tests, 0 failures.
title: android: voice-pack download survives refresh and failed second download (#620 follow-up)

body:
ANZU's existing self-development worktree APIs do not direct local Qwen/Ollama workers through scheduled RFC missions. This adds an owner-controlled queue, schedule, chat tool and page that execute one revision-bound RFC at a time using ANZU's existing tool/authorization/verification agent in a separate process and development worktree.

The local coder and vision model have separate capability checks and image routing. The native Ollama adapter uses native tools/images and explicit thinking control. Repository RFCs and Drive snapshots keep stable source identities; changes revoke approval. Recurring Drive refresh requires configured ANZU MCP read-only search/fetch tools. Priority reservations block model probes and scheduled runs; external coding agents are excluded from worker delegation. Candidates are retained for review and are never automatically merged or installed.

Implements the source scope of RFC-0211. Status/acceptance details are recorded in docs/audits/2026-10-09-ollama-self-development-validation.md.

Validation: 76 focused scheduler/worktree/self-dev/coding-contract/MCP tests passed; frontend build and lint passed; rendered-page smoke had no JavaScript errors and disabled Run while resources were reserved; git diff --check passed. The full Windows suite was stopped after roughly six minutes without progress beyond approximately 5%; no full-suite pass is claimed.

Draft: the first live generic-transport smoke timed out before tool execution. After adding native Ollama transport, the retry was stopped when the owner identified Ollama and Antigravity as occupied by Grokbot priority reverse-engineering tickets. Only our test worker was stopped. Actual native-Qwen edit/test completion, live screenshot-to-vision actions, installed-sidecar execution and real continuous Drive connector sync remain unsigned. Neither shared worker session nor the installed application was replaced.

## Owner-requested Away Mode scope
RFC-0211 now specifies one-switch / “I'm AFK, go develop yourself” activation, automatic prioritized backlog selection, independent coding and North Star review, gated merge to development, and a real application build for the merge SHA. “I'm back” pauses future work. Grokbot's priority resource reservation remains in force.

These additions are specified but not yet implemented by this PR. The existing scheduler/worker implementation is not complete delivery of the expanded RFC. Keep this PR draft until Away Mode, review/publication/build controllers and complete acceptance evidence are implemented. This documentation update does not activate automatic merges or builds.

## Default queue and upcoming work
RFC-0211 also requires scheduler intake by default for actionable work, with one shared upcoming queue visible from a primary-shell list icon. Both the owner and ANZU can reorder pending tasks; owner ordering/pins take precedence, changes persist and support undo, and resource/dependency gates still apply. Ordinary conversation remains immediate. These queue/UI additions are specified and await implementation alongside the expanded Away Mode flow.
title: RFC-0211: ANZU-controlled local Ollama self-development scheduler

body:
ANZU previously required a manually configured external inference endpoint. It now discovers local model servers in the background and asks the owner to use, leave, stop, or replace a model, with HUD/Model-page controls and a front-lane chat/voice announcement. Startup waits for an unresolved owner choice; approved endpoints can reconnect automatically. Attachment uses the existing provider and keeps the conversation.

Discovery requires model metadata, distinguishes loaded Ollama/LM Studio instances, excludes Ollama's internal workers and ANZU's front/managed seats, and never treats an editor as a server. Stop uses verified API unload or an exact listener/PID/create-time match; busy llama slots and in-flight ANZU requests block mutations. Replacement requires successful stop verification. Unknown activity is labelled and stop/replace needs confirmation.

RFC-0210 and the accompanying review document cover the recovered owner request. The scheduler review identifies the missing repository/RFC reservation and coding-mission supervisor; it is not implemented by this PR. The manager evaluation recommends an independently packaged recovery supervisor and verified payload rollback, with optional coding diagnosis and on-demand computer use. No manager recovery model or recurring schedule is claimed implemented. No architect-owned specs changed.

Validation:
- 75 focused backend tests passed in isolated runs: 33 RFC-0210, 29 inference backend, 13 status-monitor/manager.
- Frontend TypeScript/Vite build and lint passed; existing warnings remain. `git diff --check` passed.
- Windows read-only discovery found loaded Qwen in LM Studio and `anzu-coder-27b:latest` in Ollama. No live model/process was switched or stopped.
- Full Windows suite stalled. A bounded attempt captured AnyIO/Windows event-loop creation waiting in Python `socket.socketpair()`/`accept()` during an Amazon Ads API test. Restoring the unchanged development backend integration files and repeating the full suite also stalled; a baseline isolated Amazon Ads run passed 24 tests. Full-suite acceptance remains open; logs are preserved locally.
- Installed-release smoke, real-chat handoff and audible Windows interaction remain unverified. This PR does not update the installed ANZU executable.
title: RFC-0210: Discover running models and offer owner choices
